programme.title: We Don't Need A Map
programme.desc: Filmmaker Warwick Thornton investigates our relationship to the Southern Cross, in this fun and thought-provoking ride through Australia's cultural and political landscape. He takes us on a journey through this five-star constellation's astronomical, colonial and Indigenous history to the present day. For Aboriginal people the meaning of this heavenly body is deeply spiritual. By contrast, the star-adorned Eureka Flag was emblematic of protest and defiance, a quality that caused it to be adopted by activists, and lately, the darker side of Australian nationalism.

His final years are marked by financial turmoil, isolation and declining health. A planned comeback never materialises. And long after his death, new voices emerge with troubling accounts that keep the questions surrounding his legacy very much alive.

programme.title: We Don't Need A Map
programme.desc: Filmmaker Warwick Thornton investigates our relationship to the Southern Cross, in this fun and thought-provoking ride through Australia's cultural and political landscape. He takes us on a journey through this five-star constellation's astronomical, colonial and Indigenous history to the present day. For Aboriginal people the meaning of this heavenly body is deeply spiritual. By contrast, the star-adorned Eureka Flag was emblematic of protest and defiance, a quality that caused it to be adopted by activists, and lately, the darker side of Australian nationalism.

programme.title: Blackfellas
programme.desc: Based on The Day of The Dog by Archie Weller, this film tells of an Aboriginal man caught between his allegiance to his people and his aspirations to escape a cycle of self-destructive behaviour.

programme.title: An Unfinished Life
programme.desc: Old wounds get a chance to heal when a Wyoming rancher (Robert Redford) shelters his daughter-in-law (Jennifer Lopez) and her child.

programme.title: Master Cheng (a Spice For Life)
programme.desc: Following the death of his wife, professional chef Cheng travels with his young son to a remote village in Finland to connect with an old Finnish friend he once met in Shanghai. Upon arrival, nobody in the village seems to know his friend but local cafe owner Sirkka offers him accommodation. In return Cheng helps her in the kitchen, surprising the locals with the delights of Chinese cuisine.

programme.title: The Movie Show

In a remote monastery in 1940s Australia, a mission for Aboriginal children is run by a renegade nun, Sister Eileen. A new charge is delivered in the dead of night – a boy who appears to have special powers. When the monastery takes possession of a precious relic, a large carving of Christ on the cross, the new boy encounters Jesus for the first time and is transfixed.

programme.title: We Don't Need A Map
programme.desc: Filmmaker Warwick Thornton investigates our relationship to the Southern Cross, in this fun and thought-provoking ride through Australia's cultural and political landscape. He takes us on a journey through this five-star constellation's astronomical, colonial and Indigenous history to the present day. For Aboriginal people the meaning of this heavenly body is deeply spiritual. By contrast, the star-adorned Eureka Flag was emblematic of protest and defiance, a quality that caused it to be adopted by activists, and lately, the darker side of Australian nationalism.

programme.title: We Don't Need A Map
programme.desc: Filmmaker Warwick Thornton investigates our relationship to the Southern Cross, in this fun and thought-provoking ride through Australia's cultural and political landscape. He takes us on a journey through this five-star constellation's astronomical, colonial and Indigenous history to the present day. For Aboriginal people the meaning of this heavenly body is deeply spiritual. By contrast, the star-adorned Eureka Flag was emblematic of protest and defiance, a quality that caused it to be adopted by activists, and lately, the darker side of Australian nationalism.

programme.title: Golden Boy
programme.desc: Mobsters Soni & Dzoni help find Denis another club so he can make them some money and clear Chucky's debt. Meanwhile, Denis finds out that his ex, Diana, is seeing a rival footballer and they're due to confront each other on the pitch in an upcoming match.

programme.title: We Don't Need A Map
programme.desc: Filmmaker Warwick Thornton investigates our relationship to the Southern Cross, in this fun and thought-provoking ride through Australia's cultural and political landscape. He takes us on a journey through this five-star constellation's astronomical, colonial and Indigenous history to the present day. For Aboriginal people the meaning of this heavenly body is deeply spiritual. By contrast, the star-adorned Eureka Flag was emblematic of protest and defiance, a quality that caused it to be adopted by activists, and lately, the darker side of Australian nationalism.

programme.title: Blackfellas
programme.desc: Based on The Day of The Dog by Archie Weller, this film tells of an Aboriginal man caught between his allegiance to his people and his aspirations to escape a cycle of self-destructive behaviour.

programme.title: An Unfinished Life
programme.desc: Old wounds get a chance to heal when a Wyoming rancher (Robert Redford) shelters his daughter-in-law (Jennifer Lopez) and her child.

programme.title: Master Cheng (a Spice For Life)
programme.desc: Following the death of his wife, professional chef Cheng travels with his young son to a remote village in Finland to connect with an old Finnish friend he once met in Shanghai. Upon arrival, nobody in the village seems to know his friend but local cafe owner Sirkka offers him accommodation. In return Cheng helps her in the kitchen, surprising the locals with the delights of Chinese cuisine.

programme.title: The Movie Show
programme.desc: Highlights from the Film Critics Awards Night, honouring John Seale, with wins for Sam Neill and Jane Campion. Plus reviews of Driving Miss Daisy and more.

programme.title: Alick & Albert
programme.desc: Even though they live worlds apart, Torres Strait artist and activist Alick Tipoti and His Serene Highness Prince Albert II of Monaco unite to help protect the Ocean.

In a remote monastery in 1940s Australia, a mission for Aboriginal children is run by a renegade nun, Sister Eileen. A new charge is delivered in the dead of night – a boy who appears to have special powers. When the monastery takes possession of a precious relic, a large carving of Christ on the cross, the new boy encounters Jesus for the first time and is transfixed.

programme.title: Madison

programme.title: Another Country
